title_en: China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Wuxi Branch v. China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd., Changchun Branch — case concerning jurisdictional objection over an entrustment contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: The validity of a contract is an evaluation of whether an already formed contract is lawful. A contract formed in accordance with the law only then has legal binding force on the parties. The provision of Article 57 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which states that 'the invalidity, revocation, or termination of a contract shall not affect the validity of independently existing clauses in the contract concerning the method of dispute resolution,' applies to contracts that have already been formed. The 'clauses concerning the method of dispute resolution' shall comply with the statutory conditions for formation.

full_text_en:
China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Wuxi Branch v. China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd., Changchun Branch — dispute over jurisdiction over commission contract

Ruling Summary

The validity of a contract is an evaluation of whether an already formed contract is lawful. A contract formed in accordance with the law is binding on the parties. Article 57 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the invalidity, revocation, or termination of a contract shall not affect the validity of any independently existing clause concerning the method of dispute resolution in the contract," applies to contracts that have been formed. "Clauses concerning the method of dispute resolution" must satisfy the statutory conditions for formation.

When reviewing a challenge to jurisdiction, both procedural fairness and judicial efficiency should be emphasized. The parties' right to challenge jurisdiction should be properly protected, while the misuse or abuse of such right should be promptly corrected and restrained. Jurisdiction shall be determined based on the circumstances at the time the action is filed, and the evidence submitted by the parties shall be examined in light of the claims to determine jurisdiction.

Considering the claims of both parties in the two cases, if the claims in the subsequent action are sustained, there is a possibility of substantively negating the judgment in the prior action. If the claims in the subsequent action cannot be fully encompassed within the judgment in the prior action, and the civil legal relationships underlying the claims in the two actions are not identical, the subsequent action and the prior action are not duplicative.

After a case is transferred, whether a party's claims may be resolved through a counterclaim in another case falls outside the scope of the review and handling of a jurisdictional challenge. This should be dealt with by the transferee people's court in accordance with Articles 232 and 233 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, among other relevant provisions, taking into account the parties' disposition of their right of action.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 428

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Wuxi Branch. Domicile: No. 7 and No. 9 Xueqian Street, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province.

Responsible Person: Wang Yanrong, President of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Zhai Hongtao, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Beijing).

Agent ad litem: Li Bo, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Beijing).

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd., Changchun Branch. Domicile: No. 2677 Jiefang Avenue, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Responsible Person: Wang Shoukun, President of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Gao Qiang, lawyer of Jilin Gongcheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zeng Qinghua, lawyer of Jilin Gongcheng Law Firm.

Appellant China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Wuxi Branch (hereinafter "CMB Wuxi Branch") filed an appeal with this Court against the civil ruling (2015) Su Shang Chu Zi No. 00031 of the Jiangsu High People's Court, in the case concerning the challenge to jurisdiction over the commission contract dispute with Appellee China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd., Changchun Branch (hereinafter "CEB Changchun Branch").

Plaintiff CMB Wuxi Branch filed an action with the Jiangsu High People's Court, alleging the following: On May 30, 2014, CMB Wuxi Branch (Party B) and CEB Changchun Branch (Party A) entered into a General Agreement on Cooperation for Entrusted Directed Investment Business (hereinafter the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement"), which provided: Party A deposits interbank funds with Party B and entrusts Party B to make directed investments in financial assets designated by Party A, including but not limited to bank deposits. When Party A conducts deposit business with Party B, a separate deposit agreement shall be executed. The rights and obligations under the deposit business shall be governed by the specific deposit agreement. However, Party A warrants that, regardless of the terms of the interbank deposit agreement, such terms shall not affect Party B's use of such funds as entrusted funds to conduct directed investment business externally. Any breach by Party B of the specific interbank deposit agreement resulting from its external investment under this Agreement shall be deemed a modification of the interbank deposit agreement, and Party B shall not bear any liability for breach of the interbank deposit agreement. Upon Party A's issuance of an Investment Instruction to Party B, Party A shall be deemed to have agreed to terminate the interbank deposit and to have Party B make the investment, without the need to separately execute a fund transfer agreement or issue a transfer instruction. Party A may no longer demand that Party B pay any deposit principal or interest or bear any liability under the Interbank Deposit Agreement. Party B is entitled to charge a service fee for the directed investment conducted based on Party A's instructions. The specific fee rate and payment method shall be negotiated by the parties based on the investment circumstances and shall be confirmed in the Investment Instruction and its receipt. For projects in which Party A instructs Party B to invest on its behalf, Party A shall independently assess the risks and returns of the investment project and the legal risks of all contracts and documents to be executed by Party B on Party A's behalf, and shall bear the corresponding investment risks, legal risks, operational risks, and compliance risks. Any dispute arising in connection with this Agreement shall be settled through negotiation between the parties. If negotiation fails, the parties agree to submit the dispute to the court in the place where Party B is located for litigation.

At the same time, the parties entered into a Financial Institution Fixed Term Interbank Deposit Agreement (hereinafter the "Interbank Deposit Agreement"), which provided: CEB Changchun Branch opens a fund deposit account with CMB Wuxi Branch for fund placement. The deposit amount is RMB 350 million, the deposit term is 364 days, the value date shall be the date the funds are credited, and the deposit interest rate is 6.2% per annum. On the same day, CEB Changchun Branch deposited RMB 350 million into the designated account. However, CMB Wuxi Branch did not formally deliver a certificate of account opening or a debit memo to CEB Changchun Branch as required by the Interbank Deposit Agreement, and CEB Changchun Branch raised no objection.

During this period, CEB Changchun Branch issued an Investment Instruction to CMB Wuxi Branch, entrusting CMB Wuxi Branch to transfer the entrusted funds into a custodian account through the "Zhongshan-Zhaoshang Wuxi No. 1 Directed Asset Management Plan Asset Management Contract" (hereinafter the "Zhongshan-Zhaoshang Asset Management Contract") entered into with Zhongshan Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Zhongshan Securities"); CMB Wuxi Branch, by entering into the Zhongshan-Zhaoshang Asset Management Contract with Zhongshan Securities, had Zhongshan Securities, on behalf of the directed asset management plan, extend an entrusted loan to Ping An Bank Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Branch (hereinafter "Ping An Bank Shenzhen Branch"). The investment amount was RMB 350 million, the investment term was from May 30, 2014 to May 29, 2015, and the investment return rate was 7.2% per annum; the agency service fee rate payable by CEB Changchun Branch to CMB Wuxi Branch was 0.5%.

Pursuant to the Investment Instruction, CMB Wuxi Branch entered into the Zhongshan-Zhaoshang Asset Management Contract with Zhongshan Securities, and issued a written instruction for Zhongshan Securities to enter into an Entrusted Loan Contract with Ping An Bank Shenzhen Branch and the actual borrower designated by CEB Changchun Branch, Liuhe Juxinyuan Rice Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Liuhe Rice Company"), in the amount of RMB 350 million. On the same day, CMB Wuxi Branch deposited RMB 350 million into the account of Zhongshan Securities at CMB Wuxi Branch. Zhongshan Securities subsequently entered into the Entrusted Loan Contract with Ping An Bank Shenzhen Branch and Liuhe Rice Company, and ultimately disbursed the RMB 350 million loan to Liuhe Rice Company. Now, Liuhe Rice Company is unable to repay the principal and interest of the RMB 350 million loan under the Entrusted Loan Contract. CEB Changchun Branch, in violation of the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement, demands that CMB Wuxi Branch repay the deposit principal and interest under the Interbank Deposit Agreement.

CMB Wuxi Branch prayed for judgment: 1. Confirm that the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement is legal and valid; 2. Order CEB Changchun Branch to continue performing the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement and to bear all losses resulting from the investment; 3. Confirm that the Interbank Deposit Agreement has been terminated and is not binding on the parties; 4. Order CEB Changchun Branch to pay CMB Wuxi Branch an agency service fee of RMB 1.75 million under the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement; 5. Order CEB Changchun Branch to bear the litigation costs.

After the Jiangsu High People's Court accepted the case on September 6, 2015, the defendant, CEB Changchun Branch, raised a challenge to jurisdiction within the time limit for submitting its statement of defense at first instance, primarily on the following grounds: 1. The Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement and the Investment Instruction submitted by CMB Wuxi Branch are both forgeries; the seal of CEB Changchun Branch and the name stamp of its legal representative affixed thereto are counterfeit. CEB Changchun Branch and CMB Wuxi Branch never entered into or performed the aforementioned agreements, and there is no agreement on jurisdiction. Therefore, CMB Wuxi Branch cannot rely on the jurisdiction clause in the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement to file this action in the people's court at CMB Wuxi Branch's domicile. CMB Wuxi Branch's claims against CEB Changchun Branch regarding the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement and the Investment Instruction, seeking confirmation of the validity of the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement and its continued performance, as well as the claim for payment of agency fees based on that agreement, can only be subject to the jurisdiction of the people's court at the defendant's domicile, i.e., the Jilin High People's Court. 2. CMB Wuxi Branch's claim seeking confirmation that the Interbank Deposit Agreement has been terminated pertains to the same facts and legal relationship as the performance action previously initiated by CEB Changchun Branch based on that agreement before the Jilin High People's Court, and the claims are mutually negating. They cannot be separately adjudicated in two actions; they can only be raised as a defense or counterclaim in the performance action first initiated by CEB Changchun Branch. Therefore, CMB Wuxi Branch's filing of this action constitutes duplicative litigation. Pursuant to Article 36 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter the "Civil Procedure Law Interpretation"), this case should be transferred to the Jilin High People's Court, where the action was first filed. 3. CMB Wuxi Branch, knowing that the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement was forged and that CEB Changchun Branch had already filed an action with the Jilin High People's Court, nonetheless filed this duplicative action, constituting an abuse of procedural rights. CMB Wuxi Branch's loss of RMB 350 million resulted from the fraud of Liu Xiaoyi, Zhang Lei, and others who forged the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement and Investment Instruction. CMB Wuxi Branch has reported the case to the public security authorities, and the criminal case is currently being tried by the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province. CMB Wuxi Branch has already raised a jurisdictional challenge to the action filed by CEB Changchun Branch based on the Interbank Deposit Agreement, and has appealed after the Jilin High People's Court dismissed its challenge. Therefore, CMB Wuxi Branch's filing of this action constitutes an abuse of procedural rights and should be dismissed. In conclusion, CEB Changchun Branch requested that this case be transferred to the Jilin High People's Court for trial.

The Jiangsu High People's Court found the following facts: The Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement numbered Everbright-Zhaoshang-20140526, dated May 30, 2014, indicates Party A as CEB Changchun Branch and Party B as CMB Wuxi Branch. Article 13 of the Agreement provides that all disputes in connection with this Agreement shall be settled through negotiation; if negotiation fails, the parties agree to submit the dispute to the court in the place where Party B is located for litigation. The Agreement bears the seal of CEB Changchun Branch and the name stamp of its legal representative Wang Shoukun. According to forensic examinations conducted by the Jilin Provincial Gongzheng Judicial Appraisal Center and the Wuxi Municipal Public Security Bureau Material Evidence Appraisal Institute, the impressions of CEB Changchun Branch's seal and Wang Shoukun's name stamp on the Agreement were not made by the same seals as the sample impressions submitted for comparison.

On May 30, 2014, CMB Wuxi Branch and CEB Changchun Branch entered into an Interbank Deposit Agreement numbered 20140530-1, which provided: CEB Changchun Branch opens a fund deposit account with CMB Wuxi Branch for fund placement. The deposit amount is RMB 350 million, the deposit term is 364 days, the value date shall be the date the funds are credited, and the deposit interest rate is 6.2% per annum. Article 9 of the Agreement provides that the parties agree that any dispute arising under this Agreement shall first be settled through friendly negotiation; if negotiation fails, the parties may submit the dispute to a court with jurisdiction in either party's place of domicile through legal channels.

In June 2015, CEB Changchun Branch filed an action with the Jilin High People's Court based on the Interbank Deposit Agreement, seeking a judgment ordering CMB Wuxi Branch to pay deposit principal of RMB 350 million plus deposit interest and liquidated damages. The Jilin High People's Court accepted the case on July 2, 2015, under case number (2015) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 16. CMB Wuxi Branch subsequently raised a challenge to jurisdiction. On August 3, 2015, the Jilin High People's Court issued a civil ruling (2015) Ji Min Guan Chu Zi No. 4, dismissing CMB Wuxi Branch's jurisdictional challenge. CMB Wuxi Branch, dissatisfied with that ruling, filed an appeal, and that case is still pending.

It was also found that on August 13, 2014, CMB Wuxi Branch reported to the Economic Crime Investigation Detachment of the Wuxi Municipal Public Security Bureau that Zhang Lei and others from CEB Changchun Branch had forged official seals, entered into the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement in the name of CEB Changchun Branch, and defrauded RMB 350 million in loans for Liuhe Rice Company's Liu Xiaoyi through the "asset management channel" of Ping An Bank Shenzhen Branch. On August 14, 2014, the Direct Subordinate Branch of the Wuxi Municipal Public Security Bureau opened a criminal investigation.

On May 22, 2015, the Wuxi Municipal People's Procuratorate of Jiangsu Province issued an indictment (Xi Jian Su Xing Su [2015] No. 36) to the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province in the case of defendants Liu Xiaoyi and Zhang Lei suspected of contract fraud. The facts found include: "Between May 23 and May 30, 2014, Zhang Lei transferred RMB 350 million from CEB Changchun Branch to CMB Wuxi Branch, and provided to CMB Wuxi Branch a forged Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement and Investment Instruction bearing counterfeit seals of CEB Changchun Branch's official seal and legal representative's name stamp, as well as forged documents such as CEB Changchun Branch's credit approval and investigation report on Liuhe Rice Company. Accordingly, CMB Wuxi Branch transferred the aforementioned RMB 350 million to Ping An Bank Shenzhen Branch through Zhongshan Securities in accordance with the Agreement. On May 30, 2014, Liu Xiaoyi and others, carrying forged purchase contracts and company documents, entered into the Entrusted Loan Contract with Ping An Bank Shenzhen Branch. Ping An Bank Shenzhen Branch disbursed RMB 350 million to the loan account opened by Liuhe Rice Company with the bank. Liu Xiaoyi arranged for all funds to be transferred to an account of Beijing New Grain Oil Industry and Trade Co., Ltd., which he actually controlled, and used the funds to repay private loans, bank loans, and invest in futures." The criminal case is still pending.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held: Article 34 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that "parties in a dispute over a contract or other property rights and interests may, by written agreement, choose the people's court at the defendant's domicile, the place of performance of the contract, the place of signing of the contract, the plaintiff's domicile, the place where the subject matter is located, or any other place actually connected with the dispute to exercise jurisdiction, provided that such choice does not violate the provisions of this Law on hierarchical jurisdiction and exclusive jurisdiction." The law confers on the parties the right to choose the court of jurisdiction, but such choice must be based on the parties' true intention. If an agreement submitted by one party is not genuine, it is not effective against the other party. In this case, Plaintiff CMB Wuxi Branch relied on the clause in the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement, which provides that "the parties agree to submit the dispute to the court at CMB Wuxi Branch's domicile for litigation," to assert that this court has jurisdiction over the case. However, according to forensic examinations conducted by the Jilin Provincial Gongzheng Judicial Appraisal Center and the Wuxi Municipal Public Security Bureau Material Evidence Appraisal Institute, the impressions of CEB Changchun Branch's seal and its legal representative Wang Shoukun's name stamp on the Agreement were not made by the same seals as the sample impressions submitted. The conclusions of these examinations are true, lawful, and admissible as evidence. Based on these conclusions, it can be established that the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement was entered into by Zhang Lei using a forged seal of CEB Changchun Branch and a forged stamp of its legal representative. The Agreement does not represent the true intention of CEB Changchun Branch and is not effective against it. Although CMB Wuxi Branch relied on Article 57 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the invalidity, revocation, or termination of a contract shall not affect the validity of any independently existing clause concerning the method of dispute resolution in the contract," to assert that the jurisdiction clause in the Agreement is independently valid, this provision of the Contract Law is premised on the objective authenticity of the contract having been confirmed by the parties, even though the contract is invalid. Therefore, this provision does not apply to this case. As for whether the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement is effective against CEB Changchun Branch due to Zhang Lei's conduct constituting apparent authority, this is a matter of legal determination in the substantive trial of the case, and there is no logical contradiction with this court's current determination that the Agreement is not effective against CEB Changchun Branch based on the forgery of the seals.

Since the jurisdiction clause in the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement is not effective against CEB Changchun Branch, the determination of the court having jurisdiction over this case shall be made in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Article 23 of the Civil Procedure Law provides that "an action arising from a contract dispute shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the defendant's domicile or the place of performance of the contract." Since the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement at issue does not represent the true intention of CEB Changchun Branch, there is no issue of performance of the Agreement. Therefore, the court with jurisdiction over this case shall be determined based on the defendant's domicile. Pursuant to Article 2 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Standards for the First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases under the Jurisdiction of High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts [Fa Fa (2015) No. 7], the Jilin High People's Court has jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases involving an amount in dispute of not less than RMB 50 million and where one party's domicile is not within its jurisdiction. The principal amount in this case is already RMB 350 million, and one party, CMB Wuxi Branch, has its domicile in Jiangsu. Therefore, this case should be under the jurisdiction of the Jilin High People's Court as the first instance court.

Furthermore, CEB Changchun Branch had previously filed an action with the Jilin High People's Court in June 2015 based on the Interbank Deposit Agreement, and that court had accepted the case. Although CMB Wuxi Branch's filing of this action does not constitute duplicative litigation under Article 247 of the Civil Procedure Law Interpretation, the two cases share the same parties and are based on substantially the same underlying facts. In that case, CMB Wuxi Branch will inevitably raise the content of the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement as a defense to its non-liability under the Interbank Deposit Agreement. The claims CMB Wuxi Branch seeks to assert based on the Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement could also be resolved through a counterclaim in that case. Therefore, it is appropriate for the two cases to be tried by the same people's court to facilitate the ascertainment of facts, save judicial resources, and unify the standards of judicial determination and adjudication. Accordingly, it is also appropriate to transfer this case to the Jilin High People's Court for consolidated trial.

In summary, CEB Changchun Branch's jurisdictional challenge is well-founded. The arguments of CMB Wuxi Branch in opposition to CEB Changchun Branch's jurisdictional challenge are not supported. Pursuant to Articles 23, 36, and 127 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows: The jurisdictional challenge raised by Defendant CEB Changchun Branch is sustained, and this case is transferred to the Jilin High People's Court for trial.

Appellant China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch, dissatisfied with the ruling, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. Although the official seal affixed to the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" in this case is inconsistent with the seal recorded for China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch, the first-instance court directly concluded that the agreement is not binding on China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch without excluding the possibility that China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch may have used such seal on other occasions or that it may have actually performed the agreement sealed with the non-recorded seal. This conclusion lacks factual and legal basis. Moreover, an official seal is only one piece of evidence proving the parties' true intention, not the sole evidence. When a dispute arises between the parties over the agreement, the court should comprehensively determine whether the parties had and expressed a true intention to enter into the contract based on factors such as the negotiation process, the authority of the personnel involved in concluding the contract, and subsequent performance. 2. Even if the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" was sealed with a non-recorded seal, whether such an agreement is valid ultimately involves the substantive issue of whether the contract handler, Zhang Lei, constituted apparent authority. The first-instance court, on one hand, held that the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" is not binding on China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch, but on the other hand, stated that if Zhang Lei's conduct constituted apparent authority, the agreement would be binding on Changchun Branch. This is contradictory. 3. Whether the jurisdiction clause in the agreement can serve as the basis for determining jurisdiction should be addressed before determining the authenticity and validity of the agreement. The jurisdiction clause in the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" is not affected by the validity of the agreement. Pursuant to Article 57 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "The invalidity, revocation, or termination of a contract shall not affect the validity of any independently existing clause in the contract concerning the method of dispute resolution," the jurisdiction clause is independent, and even if the contract is invalid, the binding force of the jurisdiction clause in the invalid contract is not affected. Regardless of the validity of the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" in this case, the validity of its jurisdiction clause is not affected. 4. According to judicial interpretations, if the place of performance is not agreed upon or is unclear, and the subject matter of the dispute is the payment of money, the place where the recipient of the money is located is the place of contract performance. The main claim in this case is for China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch to pay agency fees of RMB 1.75 million. Even if the jurisdiction clause in the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" is not applicable to this case, this case should still be under the jurisdiction of the first-instance court. 5. The claims of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch cannot be realized through a counterclaim or defense in the other case. The criminal case involving Zhang Lei, an employee of China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch, is being tried by the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court. Having this case under the jurisdiction of a People's Court in Jiangsu Province would facilitate the ascertainment of relevant facts. In summary, China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch requests that this case be tried by the Jiangsu High People's Court.

China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch submitted a written defense, arguing: 1. The "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" involved in this case is a false contract concluded by a criminal element using a fake seal to deceive China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch. This fact is confirmed by relevant expert conclusions and also determined by the criminal judgment of the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court. 2. The system of apparent authority is an exception regarding the determination of contract validity and can only be confirmed through substantive trial. Given that the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" has been determined to be false in this case, the People's Court can only presume that there is no entrustment contract or valid jurisdiction agreement between the parties. 3. The "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" involved in this case does not actually exist, and its contractual clauses (including the so-called "clause concerning the method of dispute resolution") also do not exist. Naturally, there is no need to consider the authenticity or validity of the agreement. The first-instance ruling is legally sound. 4. The "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" involved in this case was not actually performed, and there is no place of performance of the contract. This case can only be under the jurisdiction of the Jilin High People's Court, which has jurisdiction over the defendant's domicile. 5. The first-instance ruling does not deny the right of action that China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch enjoys according to law. The so-called "inability to file a counterclaim or raise a defense" claimed by China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch does not exist. The final conviction and sentencing of Zhang Lei and others are irrelevant to this case and should not affect the determination of jurisdiction in this case. In summary, the first-instance ruling is correct and should be upheld.

Opinion of the Court: Based on the appeal and defense opinions of both parties in this case, the issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: 1. The validity of the jurisdiction clause in the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement". 2. Whether the first-instance court has jurisdiction. 3. Whether the claims of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch can be resolved through a counterclaim and whether the jurisdiction of this case can be determined based on the criminal case.

1. Regarding the validity of the jurisdiction clause in the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement"

China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch filed this lawsuit with the People's Court and submitted materials including the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement", "Interbank Deposit Agreement", and "Investment Instruction", all dated May 30, 2014. According to the appraisal by the Jilin Provincial Justice Forensic Center and the Material Evidence Identification Institute of the Wuxi Public Security Bureau, the seals of China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch and the name seal of its legal representative, Wang Shoukun, affixed at the end of the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" and the "Investment Instruction" were not formed by the same seals as the sample impressions submitted. China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch has no objection to this appraisal conclusion. China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch did not submit evidence to the People's Court that China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch used the "official seal" affixed to the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" on other occasions. Therefore, it cannot be determined that the "official seal" on the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" is genuine.

Contract validity is an evaluation of the legality of a contract that has already been established. A contract established according to law is binding on the parties. There is no issue of contract validity before the contract is established. Article 57 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "The invalidity, revocation, or termination of a contract shall not affect the validity of any independently existing clause in the contract concerning the method of dispute resolution," applies to contracts that have already been established. The "clause concerning the method of dispute resolution" must also genuinely exist, reflect the true intention of both parties, and be formed by consensus. China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch should submit evidence that is objectively authentic, relevant, and lawful, sufficient to prove that the "clause concerning the method of dispute resolution" it relies on meets the statutory conditions for formation. The above appraisal conclusion proves that the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" did not bear the genuine official seal or legal representative's signature seal of China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch. Therefore, the jurisdiction clause in the said agreement has a material defect in its formation requirements, and it cannot be determined that there is a valid jurisdiction clause. China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch's appeal argument that the jurisdiction clause involved is independent and that even if the contract is invalid, the binding force of the jurisdiction clause in the invalid contract is not affected cannot be established and is not supported by this Court.

Furthermore, the issue of whether the contract handler Zhang Lei's conduct constitutes apparent authority and the relationship between apparent authority and the validity of the jurisdiction agreement. At the stage of reviewing the jurisdictional objection raised by a party, emphasis is placed on procedural fairness and judicial efficiency. It is necessary to properly protect the party's right to raise a jurisdictional objection while also promptly correcting and curbing the misuse and abuse of the right to raise a jurisdictional objection. At this stage, a formal review of the evidence submitted by the parties is generally conducted in conjunction with the claims to identify the elements that determine jurisdiction, such as the plaintiff's domicile, the defendant's domicile, the place of contract performance, the place of contract signing, the location of property, the place of the tortious act, the amount in dispute, the extent of the case's influence, and whether there is a valid jurisdiction clause. Moreover, jurisdiction is determined as of the time of filing the lawsuit. Pursuant to Article 49 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "If a person enters into a contract in the name of the principal without agency authority, beyond agency authority, or after agency authority is terminated, and the counterparty has reason to believe that the person has agency authority, the agency act shall be effective," and Article 13 of the "Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil and Commercial Contract Disputes under the Current Circumstances", which provides: "The system of apparent authority as provided in Article 49 of the Contract Law requires not only that the agent's unauthorized agency act objectively creates an appearance of authority, but also that the counterparty subjectively, in good faith and without negligence, believes that the person has agency authority. The counterparty claiming the establishment of apparent authority bears the burden of proof, and must not only prove that the agency act had objective formal elements of authorized agency, such as contract documents, official seals, and chops, but also prove that it believed in good faith and without negligence that the person had agency authority." The burden of proof for the system of apparent authority is relatively strict. At the stage of reviewing the jurisdictional objection, China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch did not submit evidence that is formally clear and unambiguous in content and without doubt or dispute to prove that it had reason to believe that Zhang Lei had the authority to enter into the jurisdiction clause, and that such clause would be binding on China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch. Therefore, it cannot claim the validity of the jurisdiction clause on the ground that apparent authority is established. Even if apparent authority were determined to be established through substantive trial, it would only concern the assumption of civil liability by the parties involved and would not affect the People's Court's handling of the jurisdictional objection. China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch's appeal argument that "the first-instance court, on one hand, held that the 'Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement' is not binding on China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch, but on the other hand, stated that if Zhang Lei's conduct constituted apparent authority, the agreement would be binding on Changchun Branch. This is contradictory," confuses the different tasks and different standards of determination at different stages of the litigation process. This ground of appeal cannot be established.

2. Regarding whether the first-instance court has jurisdiction

When filing the lawsuit, China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch stated that on May 30, 2014, China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch deposited RMB 350 million into the designated account, but China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch did not formally deliver the deposit certificate or the entry voucher as required by the "Interbank Deposit Agreement". The first-instance court correctly protected the right of action of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch in filing this lawsuit. Whether the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" was actually performed can only be determined through substantive trial of the case. It cannot yet be determined whether the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" was actually performed. Therefore, the appeal argument of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch that "According to judicial interpretations, if the place of performance is not agreed upon or is unclear, and the subject matter of the dispute is the payment of money, the place where the recipient of the money is located is the place of contract performance. The main claim in this case is for China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch to pay agency fees of RMB 1.75 million. Even if the jurisdiction clause in the 'Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement' is not applicable to this case, this case should still be under the jurisdiction of the first-instance court" is not supported. The first-instance court does not have jurisdiction over this case. The first-instance ruling's determination of the competent court based on the defendant's domicile is not improper.

3. Regarding whether the claims of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch can be resolved through a counterclaim and whether the jurisdiction of this case can be determined based on the criminal case

In June 2015, China Everbright Bank Changchun Branch filed another lawsuit with the Jilin High People's Court based on the "Interbank Deposit Agreement", seeking an order for China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch to pay principal of RMB 350 million in deposits plus deposit interest and liquidated damages. The Jilin High People's Court accepted the case first. Thereafter, China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch filed this lawsuit. Considering the claims of both parties in the two cases, if the claims in the later-filed action are established, there is a possibility of substantially negating the result of the earlier judgment. However, the claims of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch cannot be entirely encompassed within the result of the earlier judgment. The civil legal relationships underlying the claims in the later and earlier actions are not entirely the same. Therefore, the first-instance ruling's determination that China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch's filing of this lawsuit does not constitute a duplicative lawsuit under Article 247 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China is correct.

Pursuant to Article 36 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "If a People's Court discovers that a case it has accepted does not fall within its jurisdiction, it shall transfer the case to the People's Court that has jurisdiction. The receiving People's Court shall accept the case." A People's Court without jurisdiction may rule to transfer the case to a People's Court that has jurisdiction. Whether the plaintiff's claims in this case can be resolved through a counterclaim in the other case is beyond the scope of review and handling of a jurisdictional objection. This matter should be handled by the receiving People's Court in accordance with the relevant provisions of Articles 232, 233, etc. of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, taking into account the parties' disposition of their right of action and other circumstances. Therefore, this Court will not hear the appeal argument of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch that its claims cannot be realized through a counterclaim or defense in the other case. The first-instance ruling's determination that the claims asserted by China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch based on the "Entrusted Directed Investment Agreement" could also be resolved through a counterclaim in that case exceeds the scope of review, and this Court corrects it.

Whether this case involves a related criminal case being tried by the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province is not a statutory reason for determining civil jurisdiction. The argument of China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch that this case should be tried by the Jiangsu High People's Court on this ground cannot be established.

In summary, the appeal arguments of the appellant, China Merchants Bank Wuxi Branch, cannot be established and are not supported by this Court. The first-instance ruling is correct and should be upheld. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (1) and Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original ruling is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
